hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Find the longest contiguous sequences of available cinema seats where free equals one.

hints.title: Islands Identification
hints.text: Subtract row number from seat identifier for all free seats to form identical group identifiers across contiguous sequences.

hints.title: Rank and Output
hints.text: Group by the generated island identifier to compute minimum seat, maximum seat, and sequence length. Rank groups descending by length and output tied longest sequences.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH FreeSeats AS (
  SELECT 
    seat_id, 
    seat_id - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY seat_id) AS group_id 
  FROM Cinema 
  WHERE free = 1
), 
RankedFreeSeats AS (
  SELECT 
    MIN(seat_id) AS first_seat_id, 
    MAX(seat_id) AS last_seat_id, 
    COUNT(*) AS consecutive_seats_len, 
    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS seat_rank 
  FROM FreeSeats 
  GROUP BY group_id 
) 
SELECT 
  first_seat_id, 
  last_seat_id, 
  consecutive_seats_len 
FROM RankedFreeSeats 
WHERE seat_rank = 1 
ORDER BY first_seat_id ASC;
```

variables: N: total seats in Cinema table
complexity.notes: Row number generation, grouping, and rank ordering.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Self-joining arbitrary seat ranges causes quadratic time complexity.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(N) intermediate table for window rank calculation.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Apply the classic gaps-and-islands technique using seat_id - ROW_NUMBER().
